messages.content: 你能使用 get_stock_prices 函數來檢索蘋果、微軟、亞馬遜和特斯拉分別在1週、2週、3週和1個月的時間範圍內的股價嗎？。

function.name: get_stock_prices
function.description: Retrieves stock prices for specified companies and duration. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

companies.description: List of companies to retrieve stock prices for.

duration.description: Time duration to retrieve stock prices for. E.g., '1 week', '2 weeks', '1 month', etc.

message.reasoning:
The user wants to use the get_stock_prices function to retrieve stock prices for Apple, Microsoft, Amazon, Tesla for durations 1 week, 2 weeks, 3 weeks, 1 month. The function signature expects companies: string[], duration: string. But we need to call it multiple times? The user says "retrieves stock prices for specified companies and duration". They want separate durations for each company? Actually they say "for Apple, Microsoft, Amazon and Tesla respectively in 1 week, 2 weeks, 3 weeks and 1 month time ranges." That implies Apple: 1 week, Microsoft: 2 weeks, Amazon: 3 weeks, Tesla: 1 month. So we need to call get_stock_prices four times with different parameters.

We should produce calls to the function. According to guidelines, we can only call one function at a time. We need to decide which call to make first. Probably start with Apple 1 week. Then after receiving response, proceed to next. But we can also combine? The function only accepts one duration per call. So we need separate calls.

Thus we will call get_stock_prices with companies ["Apple"] and duration "1 week". Then after response, call again with ["Microsoft"], "2 weeks", etc.

But the user asked to retrieve all at once. We could do multiple calls. We'll do sequential calls. We'll output the function call for Apple first.
